title: Wudu in detail
hook: the required parts: face, arms to elbows, wiping the head, feet, and the sunnah additions

segments.voice: Yesterday, shurut, the conditions, and your line: ready before the takbir. Did you check that you'd arrived before something you started? One condition was being clean. Today, how. Day one thousand seventy-four.

Uthman ibn Affan, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, asks for a vessel of water. Humran, who reports the scene, is watching. Uthman isn't about to explain anything. He's about to show it. He pours water over his hands, three times. He dips his right hand in and rinses his mouth and his nose. He washes his face, three times. His arms up to the elbows. He passes his wet hands over his head. He washes his feet up to the ankles. Then he says: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ make wudu just like this. Sahih al-Bukhari keeps the scene, at number 159. A lesson taught with water instead of words.
screen: `A VESSEL OF WATER, SOMEONE WATCHING.` → `HANDS, MOUTH, NOSE, FACE, ARMS, HEAD, FEET.` → `I SAW HIM DO IT LIKE THIS.`

segments.voice: Uthman's demonstration holds two layers, and the fiqh books separate them. The first layer is in the Qur'an itself, 5:6, in Pickthall's translation: "O ye who believe! When ye rise up for prayer, wash your faces, and your hands up to the elbows, and lightly rub your heads and (wash) your feet up to the ankles." Face, arms, head, feet. These are the required parts, the ones without which the wudu isn't done. The second layer is everything else Uthman showed: washing the hands first, rinsing the mouth and the nose, starting with the right side, doing the washings three times. Other reports add wiping the ears. These are the sunnah additions, what the Prophet ﷺ did, and Muslims follow them as part of doing it well. Inside that verse the schools read some words differently, and they say so openly. How much of the head must be wiped? The schools give different answers. And the feet: Sunni schools read the verse as washing them; Shia jurists read it as wiping them. Each reads the same Arabic carefully and arrives at its own practice. Notice how the verse itself is built. It doesn't say be pure in general. It names a face, two arms, a head, two feet. Purity, here, goes limb by limb, and the hadith adds something to that. Uthman closed by reporting that whoever makes wudu like this and then prays two units without letting the mind wander has past sins forgiven. So the washing points forward to a prayer with attention, the outer water and the inner focus treated as one movement.
screen: `THE VERSE: FACE, ARMS, HEAD, FEET.` · `THE SUNNAH: HANDS, MOUTH, NOSE, EARS.` · `THE SCHOOLS READ SOME WORDS DIFFERENTLY.` · `LIMB BY LIMB, THEN A FOCUSED PRAYER.` · then, large: `WASH YOUR FACES, AND YOUR HANDS UP TO THE ELBOWS.`

segments.voice: The practice: make wudu slowly, naming each part. If you're near water and you make wudu, go now and name each limb under your breath as you wash it: hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head, ears, feet. If you don't make wudu, you can still follow it where you sit: rest your attention on your hands, then your face, then your forearms, then the top of your head, then your feet. One part at a time, no rushing ahead. Let each one be finished before the next. The bell holds the time.
Wudu in detail. The required parts from the verse, face, arms, head, feet, and the sunnah around them, as Uthman showed. Today's word.

Your line: each limb washed. Today, the next time you wash your hands, give it your full attention, from wrist to fingertips, as if someone were watching to learn. Tomorrow, what breaks wudu. Day one thousand seventy-four.

howItsDone: Muslims make wudu before prayer by washing the face, the arms to the elbows, wiping the head, and washing or wiping the feet as their school teaches, usually adding the sunnah steps: hands, mouth, nose and ears, right before left.

notes: Pickthall 5:6 quoted from memory, matching earlier days on this path; confirm exact wording including '(wash)'.

Uthman's wudu: Sahih al-Bukhari 159 (some numberings 164), narrated by Humran; also Muslim 226. Confirm number and the details used (hands three times, mouth and nose, face and arms three times, wiping the head, feet to the ankles three times; the reward for two units prayed without the mind wandering). Wiping the ears is from other narrations, not this one; confirm it may be listed among the sunnah additions.
Sunni washing vs Shia (Ja'fari) wiping of the feet, and differences over how much of the head is wiped, stated without ranking; confirm the wording is fair to both.
Bukhari's demonstration may vary between rinsing mouth and nose 'three times'; the script does not give a count for those.
